True meaning of Yoga is the complete ending of mind's distractions.
author: Sri M

text: A yogi doesn't ask for anything. He only asks to go closer to the Supreme, to the Divine. He doesn't ask for anything because he follows the logic that God knows, there's nothing to ask.
author: Sri M

text: The whole universe is supposed to be a sankalpa of the Supreme Being and we have been in some way given the capacity to make sankalpas.
author: Sri M

text: The mind indeed is a powerful tool because it has the capacity to visualize, to think by the essence, which is the Supreme Consciousness. It has the capacity to achieve what it wants.
author: Sri M

text: The capacity of the mind, to think, to be aware, to be conscious, comes from the source, which is the Supreme Reality itself. So, when the mind thinks continuously of something, generally it becomes a fact.
author: Sri M

text: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali say, ‘Yogas chitta vritti nirodha.’ The process of Yoga is to stop the continuous distractions of the mind. Practically, it’s Yoga; theoretically, it’s Vedanta because Yoga is a way to experience what has been described in Vedanta.
author: Sri M

text: A distracted mind is the main reason that causes energy loss. So, when the mind is calm, energy is gathered. Now this energy can be used for any constructive activity, service before self.
author: Sri M

text: The human mind and the ego are intrinsically, by nature, conditioned and not infinite. You can move as close as you can to the Divine by removing as much conditionings as possible to make the mind pure. When you are that close to it, then it’s like the Sun. It burns you off. Then, you are not there.
author: Sri M

text: Whether on the path of self-realization or not, things will happen at the right time. Keep working; patience is of essence.
author: Sri M

text: When internal churning is going on, that’s the time when you should not fall victim to it or get addicted to it. Instead, watch it, and it will subside.
author: Sri M

text: The little joys we find in day-to-day life are the most wonderful things that the world can offer us. Beside these, we should remember that the lasting happiness we seek is not found outside oneself, in material things.
author: Sri M

text: One can come back to worldly life after the initial period of solitude and lead a life which is in appearance, to all intents and purposes, the same to other people. But deep down, one is a changed person and the absolute peace and happiness within is reflected in one’s dealings with the outside world.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual journey is all about this process of finding one’s true self, one’s true consciousness which is unalloyed happiness, independent of anything in the outside world.
author: Sri M

text: One has to start somewhere and that starting point is not far away but right here and now. One can start with ten minutes of introspection daily and then slowly proceed to the more important and intricate aspects of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Sādhanā is not just about meditation. It has to be complemented by one’s activity in the external world. It has to do with how one deals with other human beings. So there is more to Sādhanā than merely sitting, closing one’s eyes and pretending to meditate.
author: Sri M

text: Being kind, being helpful, and serving others is indeed worship of that divine spark resident in other beings. Kindness and doing good should go hand-in-hand with one’s meditative practices.
author: Sri M

text: Merely by taking flowers and gifts to a Guru, one should not suppose that one is moving towards one's spiritual goal. That can happen only when teachings are followed and one remains with the teacher to understand what he is trying to teach and try consciously to change one’s life according to his instructions.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t keep any secrets from your spiritual teacher. It is only through understanding the student completely that the teacher can give complete attention and lead you to a complete cure from the disease of ignorance.
author: Sri M

text: Consider it your spiritual right to meet the teacher, to talk with him and in general, lead a life of companionship with the teacher, at least for a short time. While not forgetting that he is not what he appears to be, which is an outward manifestation of the inner realization, complete spiritual perfection.
author: Sri M

text: Guru Purnima is for paying your respect to all Teachers and Gurus, both in the inner as well as the outer world. You should not imagine that we are paying respect to one Guru. It is actually to show our deep respects and love for the teacher who has brought us from darkness into light.
author: Sri M

text: While it’s true that a person who has advanced spiritually possesses certain extraordinary capacities, it is also true that a genuine spiritual teacher as far as possible does not exhibit his powers simply for the reason that a genuine seeker is not interested in his powers,miracles, protection or anything of this kind.
author: Sri M

text: I think to seek power from the spiritual teacher is merely a carryover, an extension of seeking power and luxuries from this world into the spiritual field. I would call it spiritual entertainment and I think no genuine spiritual Guru should be wasting his time and energy performing these wonders and diverting the genuine aspirant's mind.
author: Sri M

text: The moment you are serious that nothing else is more important to you than finding the Truth; your Guru will come to you. One of the main functions of the Guru is to make you stand on your own feet. A true Guru does not want you to be dependent on anybody. He wants you ultimately to flower, become free and not to bind you even to himself.
author: Sri M

text: Why do we study Advaita, Brahma Sutras, Upanishads, and practice Kriya Yoga? Why do we do that? Because we feel inadequate, and we want to touch that completeness from which we have come, the Source.
author: Sri M

text: From birth onwards, when we begin to learn, we are conditioned into believing that we are weak and incapable of doing certain things. But the great message of the Upanishads is “Uttishthata jagrata prapya varan nibodhata”, meaning Arise, Awake and Stop not till the goal is reached.
author: Sri M

text: There is nothing impossible on this earth if one puts his or her mind to it. Why? Because, Inside us is the essence of that Purnata, our true essence.
author: Sri M

text: Adi Shankaracharya said that ultimately there is only One reality, not two. All dissipation, all problems, all tensions happen when there is another. There is only One, and that reality happens to be you.
author: Sri M

text: Thoughts can be constructive, but thoughts can also be damaging. When thoughts have subsided, infinite energy flows into you. A Yogi or Vedantin is one who deliberately works out techniques to tap the energy within.
author: Sri M

text: If you practice Kriya and if one’s foremost intention is not finding the Truth, then even Kriya is not going to work. The Supreme Being will not show himself if I sit down and breathe up and down ten times a day.
author: Sri M

text: There is one shortcut to finding the truth which most don't attempt as it is very difficult. And that is to cut the ego into two. Let’s leave the shortcut for now and see if we can suspend our judgement and say — let me explore and find out.
author: Sri M

text: Everything in the world comes to an end, even our happiness has an end. The great thing about spiritual realisation is that it is endless. Every day, there is unveiling and it happens in different ways. Every day is a new day.
author: Sri M

text: All knowledge is a memory, and if it is memory, it is always a thing of the past. It cannot be in the present. The present does not require memory, it's there. So, the Truth is that something which cannot be slotted into a memory. A spiritual experience is always fresh and new.
author: Sri M

text: All things that have come out of the void go back into the void. Anything here in this world is temporary; it will pass.
author: Sri M

text: When you say you have will, you also have the mind and the brain to decide what is good and what is bad. According to my understanding, anything that is harmful to others is bad, and anything that is not harmful to others is good. Anything that leads me towards my spiritual goal is good, and anything that leads me away from it is bad.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot meditate or be spiritual all twenty-four hours. So, what do you do with the rest of the time? You need to initiate some action which is good for others.
author: Sri M

text: You can shed the dross of your own mind by empathizing with others and helping them out. Gradually when the mind is purified, you are able to meditate properly.
author: Sri M

text: What is the way to convert tamoguna into sattva ? Action, so that the tamas is converted into rajas and, when rajas , action is oriented towards the good of others, it takes you into sattva and from sattva , you finally reach the state which is beyond all gunas.
author: Sri M

text: It is better to maintain a happy outlook than an unhappy one. Try to remain with a happy attitude of mind, but don't neglect the fact that this cannot be sustained until we find the inner happiness which is in us.
author: Sri M

text: Break free from all bondage, realize that your true self is ever free and never bound! This was the clarion call of the great and ancient Upanishadic teaching - Moksha, Moksha, Moksha!
author: Sri M

text: If you learn the art of being one pointed in meditation, you are automatically in meditation all the time. If you are one-pointed in your day to day life, you are one-pointed in meditation too.
author: Sri M

text: Let go and rejoice! It doesn’t mean you should sell everything you possess and go away. It means to let go off all the things from the past and stay in the present.
author: Sri M

text: Hatha yoga deals more with the body and gets it fit to go to the next layer, the mind. Raja Yoga deals with the mind. You can say it's ‘mind yoga’, not opposed to, but complementing Hatha yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita defines Yoga as ‘Yogam karmasu kaushalam’, which means Yoga is how to work with complete tranquility and auspiciousness
author: Sri M

text: The mind is always moving up and down. Sometimes happy, sometimes sad. It is like a roller-coaster ride. Yoga is how to balance this roller-coaster movement of the mind and make it quiet.
author: Sri M

text: The guide, the teacher, or the friend who has crossed to the other side, who has learnt to swim and cross the ocean of samsara , what does he do? He teaches you how to swim so that you too can cross the ocean.
author: Sri M

text: The Yogic mind is tranquil, quiet but very alert. It’s not as if it is drugged or has gone to sleep. Intelligence works one-pointedly and sees everything. It’s not as if the eyes are shut.
author: Sri M

text: Yama Niyama are rules and regulations to be followed in life. Please don’t think Yoga is ‘another worldly’ philosophy. It is meant for us now, ‘Idam’ in this moment.
author: Sri M

text: Ahimsa means not to think evil of others or not to cause injury to other living beings to the best extent possible. If you can do that fully, you are already a Yogi.
author: Sri M

text: Can we live honestly and be truthful in our dealings? Not easy. Try your best.
author: Sri M

text: Very often when you say ' rishi ', people give it a religious connotation. Rishi is the ancient scientist who delved into the mysteries of life, figured out who and where we are, what our connection is with the world and enquired into a reality beyond what is seen.
author: Sri M

text: It's good to erase one's yesterdays and live in today. Then you are lighter; there are no burdens.
author: Sri M

text: It's more important to understand the teachings than to worship the teacher. The sacred is always around us and in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: In ancient India, the young aspirant, the neophyte, the brahmachari went to the Masters, the Rishis , seeking not wealth, not health, not position but pure and unconditioned freedom. This pure, unconditioned, unbound freedom is called moksha or mukti .
author: Sri M

text: What is spirituality? It is to find the truth, to find yourself, to find who you are, and what is your link with the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Sharing is an essential part of well-being. As you give, so you receive. So, give whenever possible, whatever possible, in whichever way you can.
author: Sri M

text: Janamashtami is a day to actually rejoice for the advent of spiritual consciousness on earth, in a very complete and all embracing form .
author: Sri M

text: Wherever you see Krishna in any picture, usually he has a flute in his hand, playing beautiful music because music is to do with the heart, it penetrates. It has nothing to do with your rational mind.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. You cannot run anywhere. So stay here and fight it out but do it with love and affection and understanding. See Krishna in everybody.
author: Sri M

text: It is good to be rational but we have to sometimes examine, if this thing that we call our rational framework, is really an absolute entity or a temporary or comparative entity.
author: Sri M

text: The only data available to all of us through the five senses is not only limited, but also sometimes misleading. It may be what we think is right but may not be right.
author: Sri M

text: If I begin something by saying "I know", then there is no enquiry whatsoever. So first I should say, "Well I don't know, let me find out." This comes only with great humility, otherwise it cannot come.
author: Sri M

text: If one has to be a 'stitha prajna', with the mind in a calm, quiet, tranquil state, we have to ‘let go’ and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Behind the personalities we have, all distinct and different, there is an inner essence of consciousness common to all, which by its very nature is blissful, free and liberating.
author: Sri M

text: True consciousness means to go beyond all images, not the images that we see around us but those we build up in our minds. It is because of these images that we get hurt.
author: Sri M

text: For anything spiritual to happen, anything to go beyond our ordinary understanding, you need to have a tranquil mind.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is open, and when there is a great desire to achieve something, then the channels for achieving that are opened.
author: Sri M

text: Kali a symbol of the whole creation, it is the reality – tongue out, blood dripping. This is reality all around us. Don’t run away from it. The ultimate sacrifice is to add your head, your ego as one of the heads that form the munda mala on her neck munda mala vibushitam.
author: Sri M

text: Ganesha represents the actual beginning of transcendence of consciousness from the gross to subtle.
author: Sri M

text: One can go close to the Truth but when we go very close, the heat and the energy are such that we no longer remain. We are totally burnt off and what remains is only the truth.
author: Sri M

text: Keep your emotions under control. In a battle like situation, you cannot be effective if you are emotionally involved.
author: Sri M

text: If one does not know the taste of a sweet, how can it be explained to others? It’s only through ‘ anubhava ’ or experience that one understands. ‘ Anubhava ’ - practising it and experiencing it is most important. No theory can help in learning.
author: Sri M

text: The search for the source cannot be positively identified. It’s only when all that is not the self is negated then only the Self remains. It's like a sculptor trying to work on an image. What does he do? He just chips away.
author: Sri M

text: Moksha and freedom should come while you are still involved in the world with maybe short periods of solitude. Running away from fear and failure is not Moksha .
author: Sri M

text: What is the Real? The Upanishads say that which is pure existence is real. Anything seen is only because of the observer. When one is free from all conditioning offered by the five senses, then one finds the world also unconditioned. The observer is the only reality.
author: Sri M

text: All the practices in any spiritual school of thought or teaching talk about cleansing. Cleansing means making the mind free of all distractions.
author: Sri M

text: Patanjali says Yoga is chitta vritti nirodha , so vritti includes thoughts, good vrittis , bad vrittis , positive vrittis , negative ones. What is intended is to be free of all vrittis.
author: Sri M

text: Sound is the beginning of everything. It is from sound that light comes, it is from sound that the entire creation takes place. The sound that we know and can link to the primordial sound is the Pranava, Om.
author: Sri M

text: Humility is an inner feeling that I am just nothing. In this vast world that is in constant movement all the time, I am a small particle like a grain of sand in the sea. The great ones know this.
author: Sri M

text: Nature has this very peculiar habit: when you run behind something, it runs away from you. If you say I am okay whether it happens or not, then it happens.
author: Sri M

text: We have many imaginary ideas about ourselves and we project them. We see ourselves as distorted, positive and negative. The function of the teacher is to clean the mirror and show it at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is about how you lead your life and how you practice. It’s not a magic technique. We have to change our lifestyles, our behavior and see how we are going, then practice Kriya. There is no such lodestone which you touch and iron becomes gold.
author: Sri M

text: When we begin to understand that ego is the root of all evil and problems, then we will know how to handle it, how to get rid of it and nip it in the bud. This is not a one-day affair.
author: Sri M

text: Is fire a symbol of sacrifice? It is! So, if you can all offer all the things that cover your inner essence into the fire, then that is a sacrifice. Every year, we light a symbolic dhuni. It says put everything in there, burn it.
author: Sri M

text: There is this spark of the divine in every one of us. There is not a single person who doesn’t have the spark inside. You just need to remove the structure and break away.
author: Sri M

text: The image one creates may be important in a profession but deep down, you should know that ‘I have put on a form. Actually, I am not this.’ From there, you go deeper and figure out the Inner Self. This is why the Upanishads declared - Tat Tvam Asi , You Are That.
author: Sri M

text: Is it possible to get rid of fear totally? If you have found your true self, you don’t have to purge out the fear because it does not exist anymore.
author: Sri M

text: A human being whose mind has become tranquil can remain peaceful even while talking a lot. It’s not the external manifestation that is important but the internal state of mind.
author: Sri M

text: The only thought that can be considered not a distraction during meditation is the thought of the deity, or the thought that I am meditating or the thought that in me, is the Supreme self.
author: Sri M

text: Tranquility is a state of mind. It’s not ‘mouna’ when the mind is seething.
author: Sri M

text: Mouna is a state of mind where the mind has become quiet and tranquil and even in the midst of all cyclones, it’s still calm.
author: Sri M

text: Do you know that nine is a symbol of Shakti because Shakti from the concept of tantra is the ever-renewing force which cannot be subtracted or added. It is always constant. Nine is the only number which however much you multiply it with any number and add the total will again give you nine. Therefore, nine represents the ever renewing, always present form of manifestation of Shakti.
author: Sri M

text: Parashakti means Supreme Energy - That which is at the beginning of time and which will remain forever, after we have come and gone. And it is that form of Shakti which is most active and kinetic, the one that dances on Shiva’s chest.
author: Sri M

text: Shakti is most important because S hivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti , without the havan kund , no homa can be done.
author: Sri M

text: From the Samayamarga point of view, Tantra is the understanding of the activity of the shakti in the human system and how to awaken it and enjoy and get drunk in that, not from outside sources.
author: Sri M

text: When you worship the Devi in Tantra, the Devi is decorated in a very beautiful way. So Soundarya Lahar i – the teachings of Tantra are more to do with aishwarya, bhakti, beauty rather than discarding everything and sitting in a cave.
author: Sri M

text: Bapu is no longer physically with us but his spirit lives in our heart and pervades all humanity. With great humility, I take the dust of Sabarmati, where he walked and spun the fabric of truth and non violence. Ram Ram. Pranam.
author: Sri M

text: In the Devi Mahatmyam , Durga is said to pervade the cosmos to create, maintain and periodically destroy it, according to the rhythms. When cosmic balance is threatened by the enemies of the Gods, though she is eternal, the goddess becomes manifest over and over again, to protect the world.
author: Sri M

text: The transformation of a human into a divine being begins when a person who knows how to operate the energies with deep devotion and love puts his attention on taking ‘shakti’ up the path to the ‘sahasrara.’
author: Sri M

text: It’s when the Kundalini energy reaches the crown that it merges with the Supreme Reality called Shivam. Shakti and Shivam become One and this ecstasy far exceeds the ecstasy any ordinary human being has ever experienced before.
author: Sri M

text: Stay with the situation, understand it properly and keep trying to overcome it. Running away and trying to come out as quickly as possible does not work with deep rooted mental suffering.
author: Sri M

text: From childhood, we are hypnotized into believing that we are limited. This is the problem. Now, what do we do? Start saying that I am the spark of that infinite supreme reality, ‘Purna is my essence. I will not stop until I reach my goal. “Prapya Varan Nibodhata, ” Believe me, it works.
author: Sri M

text: Where do we find ‘Purnata’ or complete fulfillment? It does not seem to exist in the outside world. Whatever we do, we are still not satisfied. So turn inwards, says the Upanishad. Look within, here, you will find unlimited potential for reaching ‘Purnata’.
author: Sri M

text: What is the meaning of a healthy mind? A mind which is not torn by conflict, not disturbed by any distractions whatsoever, does not overindulge, nor is it steeped in lethargy, is active but calm, quiet but sensitive. Like in the ocean, the waves come but they don’t affect you.
author: Sri M

text: It is in the nature of things that in this life, there is always some sorrow and pain. There is no uniform happiness ever possible, if our happiness is based on the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness based on an inner understanding cannot be shaken by any pain or sorrow that comes from the outside world.
author: Sri M

text: Give as much as possible, without expecting anything in return. It's a great medicine for sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: If we can look within us, through all our joys and sorrows, is what in the Vedantic language is called the nivritti marga.
author: Sri M

text: Coming together with marriage or without marriage is not 100% fool proof because two different individuals are coming together. As long as you start your journey with the understanding that I may not always be right, the other side may also be right, there is no problem.
author: Sri M

text: If we can free ourselves of the distractions through various means, then one day the mind which becomes quiet and tranquil realises that there is an inner being which is purna, complete, full of joy. And all who understand this, see only completeness in others.
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi is a state of exalted being where the mind is without fear, where the mind is completely quiet and tranquil with no distractions whatsoever. And that mind understands what Samadhi is all about.
author: Sri M

text: The ultimate essence of Yoga is that the mind is allowed to settle down and absorb itself in the essence of one’s being.
author: Sri M

text: In Vedanta, the ultimate state is called moksha , in Sankhya and Yoga the ultimate state is called Kaivalya and, in the Buddhist teachings it is called Nirvana .
author: Sri M

text: Kaivalya is from the root word kevala which means ‘only’, so when the mind is absolutely free of all dross, when there is no tension whatsoever, in that state of mind there is only One, that quiet mind no longer can be called the mind, it is Purusha .
author: Sri M

text: The mind has to be made free of distracting and opposing thoughts; thoughts which take away attention from the main process we are involved in. This is the practice of Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The concept of time is because of change. What is change? Movement. You can’t even think of time if there is no movement, there is no growth, there is no change. All change is movement.
author: Sri M

text: The only permanent ananda available to us is that which is real, as opposed to that which is here today and gone tomorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Good and evil, famous and notorious, darkness and light, positive and negative, are all in the Supreme Being and yet in its essential essence, the Supreme is not affected by the opposites.
author: Sri M

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that the mind can be a friend, but the same mind can also be an enemy. Cultivate the friendly side of your mind. Don’t give too much attention to the enemy.
author: Sri M

text: Love is the essence of all religions for it is religion that teaches us ethics, concern and compassion.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is the middle path. Krishna says it beautifully in the Gita, to Arjuna, “This Yoga is not for him who eats too much or eats too little, sleeps too much or sleeps too little”.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes peaceful, when there is wellness of mind, the recovery of the body is also accelerated.
author: Sri M

text: You may be more perceptive to what others are thinking, but if there is even a small iota of thought of causing harm or injury to others, then you are not moving on the spiritual path. Not possible.
author: Sri M

text: Different modes of philosophies in India, different darshanas have looked at Truth in different ways. But like the Rig Veda said 2000 years ago – “ Ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti ”- There is only one truth, the wise have called it by different names.
author: Sri M

text: The more you meditate, whatever be the mode of meditation and deeper you go into your inner self, you become a better human being. If this is not happening, then something is not okay.
author: Sri M

text: A person who is a real meditator, who has stepped at least beyond a certain boundary can never be cruel, can never intentionally cause harm to anybody or glorify himself.
author: Sri M

text: If spiritual development is your priority, no distraction is going to take away anything from you. You are one-pointedly there. So therefore, fix your priorities.
author: Sri M

text: There is no technique to find the Truth. It is not an engineering feat. You can, however, prepare the ground from where it is possible to take off.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is not to find the Truth, but to prepare oneself to keep the windows open so that when the breeze blows, the windows are not closed.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is not done to develop supra-mental powers, to walk on water or levitate in the air. That is not the aim of yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Aql ke madrase se uth, ishq ke maikade mein aa, Jaam-e-fana-o-bekhudi, ab to piya jo ho so ho Get up from the school of the intellect, come to the tavern of joy, intoxication. Now that you have drunk the wine of annihilation of the ego, whatever happens, let us enjoy.
author: Sri M

text: On this path, we may think that we are denying ourselves many things, but we are actually celebrating. Leaving aside the little trinkets, we find the big treasure.
author: Sri M

text: It’s only when there is pain and sorrow that human beings begin to think there may be a Divine Being somewhere. Guru Nanak Sahib said, “ Dukh me sumiran sab kare , sukh me kare na Koi .”
author: Sri M

text: Understanding the writing in the scriptures is to get a blueprint of what we are seeking.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Lay treasures in your heart where thieves do not break in and steal’ is a great statement which says, inside your heart is all the treasure that you seek. Therefore have faith that one day you will open this treasure and see the beautiful things that are hidden inside.
author: Sri M

text: In spiritual life we are trying to discover that we are a spark of the divine and if we are a spark of the divine, this spark must also be in others.
author: Sri M

text: Any work, service or any help you render to fellow human beings is sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: If spiritual progress is priority and the work you do is standing in the way, rather than stopping the search, it’s better to tailor your work in such a way that it does not interfere with your journey.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever you do, wherever you go, deep down in your mind, the first priority should be that before this bodily life ends, we need to find what we are seeking in our spiritual practice.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual teaching of the Gita was preached on a battlefield. We are in the battlefield of life. Is it possible for us to stick to the spiritual practice and continue in our Kurukshetra?
author: Sri M

text: You can live in this world and still seek your spiritual goal.
author: Sri M

text: If we can be tranquil while working, then even while working it is a kind of sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t miss the goal, keep that in mind. If you say it is possible, yes, it is possible!
author: Sri M

text: Develop the understanding that once you have surrendered to the Supreme Being, there is nothing to fear because you are in the hands of the Supreme Teacher. It is not just protection, but is also leading one in the right direction.
author: Sri M

text: There is no magic formula to keep one’s mind undistracted. When you are seriously interested in something, there are no distractions.
author: Sri M

text: If everything is destined then this jeeva would not have been brought out here to work towards salvation. The whole theory of moksha falls flat.
author: Sri M

text: It’s not as if only negative things come to you from the past. There are also positive aspects in your life which are seeds from the past.
author: Sri M

text: Karmic theory is not a theory of destiny, it is a theory of cause and effect. Therefore, we should shed all thought that everything is destined and try to move forward.
author: Sri M

text: If you keep repeating verbally, I am not this body, I am the Supreme Brahman, you will still remain the body. However, there are processes in the ancient texts that describe how to experience this. And that part is called sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: When we say faith, Shraddha or one pointed attention, it also teaches us humility that we don’t know everything. Till we know, we need to accept things as they are.
author: Sri M

text: Dharma actually means quality of a person’s mind or life. It reflects one’s qualities rather than the religion or one’s religious orientation.
author: Sri M

text: The most important thing is to keep your priorities in order, and don’t get totally caught up in the work. Do your work in such a way that it contributes to the welfare of others, sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ: welfare of all living beings.
author: Sri M

text: There is nothing to fear. The entire universe is pervaded by the blissful Supreme Being and we are a part of that. To live with this understanding is called holistic living.
author: Sri M

text: Through the practice of mysticism, whether it is Sufi, Yogic or Buddhist, one can awaken the centres that become active in deep meditation. Only when these centres are awakened, there is the possibility of looking into higher realms.
author: Sri M

text: Satsanga is a joint attempt by a group of people, a Sangha, to study the Truth, Sat.
author: Sri M

text: The flute has unique music which you cannot get from anything else. Music bridges the gap between the material and non-material.
author: Sri M

text: We all think in a certain language and may speak in another. But we think in the language in which we were brought up from childhood. Therefore, all thought, when you think, is already there in words.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot suddenly jump from tamo to sattva guna. To shake one up from tamas, you need activity. This is where Karma yoga comes in, where activity is rajo guna.
author: Sri M

text: Bhagavad Gita is the song of the lord. While you read it, listen as if you are there like Arjuna sitting there and listening.
author: Sri M

text: When everything is going fine, nobody is bothered about Bhagwan. It’s when some sorrow strikes or there is a problem that we usually call out, please help me!
author: Sri M

text: Gita, the song of the Lord, is that which, through it’s beautiful music, takes us away from sorrows, takes us to higher realms, and makes us understand the truth which is in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna says, among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda because it’s only a heart open to music that is open to feelings and emotions that can understand the message of the Gita.
author: Sri M

text: Sound is the Shabda brahman. It is the sound that takes you from the ordinary to the extraordinary.
author: Sri M

text: Sattva guna is when the mind is settled, is quiet and calm no matter what activity you are involved in, when it cannot think of evil about anybody, and can recognise only the divinity in all living beings.
author: Sri M

text: Fear and depression are of no use to a human being. At turning points in life, have faith in the inner reality in your heart and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Our minds and our sense organs are so involved in this world that we miss the essence of where they derive their power to function.
author: Sri M

text: The mind cannot stay without some attachment. So, attach yourself to the higher being with the thought- ‘I surrender to the supreme being.’
author: Sri M

text: According to the Gita, attaining the eternal state is not done by theoretically understanding the whole map, but by freeing oneself from the opposites.
author: Sri M

text: A yogi is not affected by pleasure, pain, praise or blame. Such a person free from pride and delusion, who therefore is not attached to pride or to delusion, is absorbed in his spiritual pursuits, free from the desires of the world.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is part of Prakriti, thought is also a part of it. That which is the Atman , is beyond ordinary thought, is the witness of all thought, but not involved in it.
author: Sri M

text: According to Shankara, when the Jiva sheds all its conditioning, there is only the Supreme Being, nothing else is left.
author: Sri M

text: Water is in the sea, in the river, in the pond, in our swimming pool and also in a small bowl. But you cannot run a ship in the bowl of water which we are keeping on our table. According to Ramanuja, that is the difference between Jiva and Eshwara.
author: Sri M

text: The whole teaching of Gita is also about different lives. One life you go, another life you come back, and the ultimate is when one is free of this cycle of birth and death.
author: Sri M

text: Even the striving yogi, till he reaches that goal does not understand that the Atman within is free of all this, though it witnesses everything. So, the Gita says – Move forward and then from the particular human being in the Jivatma , it comes to the universe.
author: Sri M

text: Viveka is the differentiation between what is real and what is unreal, what is permanent and what is temporary.
author: Sri M

text: When one understands what is temporary and what is permanent, then one discards the temporary and moves towards that which is permanent. This is called Vairagya .
author: Sri M

text: The only way to get rid of negativity is to bring in positivity. You can’t remove negativity by keeping on thinking about it. You can replace it with positive thinking.
author: Sri M

text: Whenever I think of preparing for a new day, for a new year, leaving behind the old, I am always reminded of the cry of John the Baptist, who declared, “Voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye, the way of the Lord! Make his path straight!”
author: Sri M

text: May the Christmas spirit not just be with us during this season but be a part of our every breath. May the love, joy & peace that we experience, be a part of us all through life.
author: Sri M

text: If you have a healthy body, you have a healthy mind, then you can meditate and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita is meant for applying the principles in daily life. If you cannot, there is no point in reading the Gita. It is not just theory, it is a practical text on how to move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Without vairagya and viveka, it is not possible to explore the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The straight and narrow path, so difficult to walk on, is what the Upanishads call shurasya dhara , walking on the edge of a razor! And yet, it’s only facing this and leading life dangerously that one makes quantum leaps into greater dimensions, a better life, a better human being.
author: Sri M

text: On New Year’s eve, take a piece of paper and note down point by point, the habits that we find in ourselves which are negative and need to be overcome. Note them down and, as you wake up to a new dawn, go through this again and begin to implement ways and means to get free of them. It can be done!
author: Sri M
